correctness.rationale: Examined the exact integral definition: quotient the free signed-cover regular path modules by the deck relation τp=−p BEFORE taking allowed-boundary chains, not homology-level anti-invariants. Deck orbits are free, the lifted directed-edge boundary is σ(uv)v−u. Without triangles, every nonbacktracking 2-path has a forbidden shortcut; absence of four-cycles ensures its forbidden coefficient cannot cancel with another common-neighbor 2-path. The only Ω2 boundaries are primitive backtracking relations e_uv+σ(uv)e_vu, reducing Ω1/im∂2 integrally to the edge module and differential Bσ. Switching signs along a spanning tree identifies all vertex classes and leaves exactly 2x=0 if any fundamental cycle is negative. The incidence rational rank is V−1 or V and the free kernel rank E−V+1 or E−V. Direct independent signed C5 Smith computations returned invariant factors (1,1,1,1) for balanced and (1,1,1,1,2) for unbalanced signings and the predicted first-kernel ranks, corroborating but not replacing the universal proof. For any negative cycle the double cover is connected so ordinary H0=Z with trivial deck action; hence homology anti-invariants vanish. No claim about H≥2 or H1 at smaller girth.
residual_risks: The particular integral deck-quotient refinement is a choice of coefficient theory, not claimed canonical or equal to deck anti-invariants after homology.

value.rationale: Determines a natural coefficient-sensitive obstruction to transferring a real signed path-homology comparison to integers, not merely a random graph rank. A natural integral refinement exhibits genuine order-two torsion and an explicit high-girth first-homology classification for all connected graphs under a clean geometric hypothesis. The local-system Smith form is elementary; substantive motivation comes from proving it is the correct low-degree quotient for a recent path-homology functor, where allowed 2-path restrictions could otherwise change H1.
residual_risks: Value is limited if existing signed-GLMY integral local-coefficient treatments already make the two-term identification automatic; no theorem about higher degrees follows.

final_claim: For finite connected simple signed graphs, integral degree-zero deck-quotient GLMY homology is Z for balanced signatures and Z/2 for unbalanced signatures, without girth assumption. Under girth at least five, H1 is free of ranks E−V+1 or E−V respectively. For unbalanced signatures, H0 of the connected double cover has no deck-anti-invariants although signed integral H0 is Z/2.
